thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated streaming tail latency detected for model redwood-v3-chat in us-west-gpu-cluster. p95=0.98s p99=6.4s. Pattern: streaming chunk hang + reconnect spikes. Paging on-call.

oncall-sre: Acknowledged, jumping in. Which hosts are showing anomalies?

olivia.eng: Quick look: heatmap pins gpu-node-128 and gpu-node-129. Telemetry shows memory ECC correctable bursts and GPU clock-gating events. Also seeing KV cache miss rate jump for long-prefix chats. No 5xx surge.

marc.infra: Host logs show thermal fan oscillation and repeated PCIe AER entries. NVML snapshot attached. Example lines: 
```
[ 45678.123] nvidia: Correctable ECC error on GPU 0: sbc count 95
[ 45679.001] kernel: pcieport 0000:af:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received, id 0x0040
[ 45679.210] nvme: nvme0q0: I/O 12345 failed, retrying
[ 45679.999] Thermal: GPU0 clock gating engaged due to junction temp 94C
```

kai.ops: Customer-facing impact? Any users complaining?

support-leo: A handful of customers report chat lags and UI spinner hangs. No total outages. Logged customer ticket CT-9002 for affected tenants and posted short status: "Investigating higher latency on streaming replies; engineering mitigating."

oncall-sre: Plan we can run now: 1) divert 50% of streaming traffic for affected model to us-east fallback cluster (cross-region spill) to preserve UX, 2) reduce max_stream_window to 6 for large-context streams on remaining nodes, 3) cordon gpu-node-128, attempt soft-reset, 4) if soft-reset fails, drain with streaming-preserve flow and quarantine node. Execute step 1 now.

olivia.eng: Pushing cross-region spill rule: 
```yaml
route: /v1/chat/stream
weights:
  redwood-v3-chat@us-west: 50
  redwood-v3-chat@us-east: 50
prefer_local: false
```
Deployed. Monitoring latency on both regions.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: traffic-split applied by olivia.eng at +0m40s

marc.infra: Attempting soft-reset on gpu-node-128: `cloudctl gpu soft-reset gpu-node-128` -> reset returned but NVML shows continued ECC correctable bursts. Soft-reset attempt 1: insufficient.

olivia.eng: After diversion p99 across product dropped from 6.4s -> 2.8s in ~90s. Cross-region spill looks effective. Still above SLO. Recommend increase east spill to 70% until node evacuated.

oncall-sre: Agreed. Also enable kv-prefetch warmup for new hot sessions in west to reduce cold-KV fetch penalty. Kai, can you flip prefetch?

kai.ops: Enabling kv-prefetch: `kv.cache.prefetch.enabled = true; kv.prefetch.window = 12` for us-west shard. Patch applied.

support-leo: Updating customers: CT-9002 updated with note: "We've routed some traffic to a nearby region and are evacuating a degraded GPU node. Expect improved latency within minutes; next update in 30m."

marc.infra: Soft-reset attempt 2 now. `cloudctl gpu soft-reset gpu-node-128 --force` -> reset fails after driver detach. Evidence of persistent hardware flake. Will prepare drain script.

olivia.eng: Additional in-flight mitigation: reduce batch_size on us-west serving pods from 16 -> 6 to reduce memory pressure during long prefixes. Applying as override to node selectors on remaining nodes.

oncall-sre: Good. Also enable streaming-keepalive tweak to shorter RTTs so reconnects are quicker: `stream.keepalive=4s` for west.

marc.infra: Active streaming sessions on gpu-node-128: 11. Will wait for sessions to drop <4 before safe drain. If sessions don't decrease in 10m, escalate to forced drain and rely on cross-region fallback.

kai.ops: Observing reconnect churn minimal. Cross-region spill + prefetch + batch reduction improved p99 to ~1.9s overall. Still monitoring West-only p99 which remains ~3.5s.

support-leo: Notifying PMs and customer success: rachel.pm tagged. Rachel, want a short blurb for comms?

rachel.pm: Yes, please prep a short post: impact summary, mitigations, expected resolution ETA. I'll review and send to customers if we breach >30m.

olivia.eng: Active sessions on node down to 3. Initiating graceful drain sequence: `./scripts/graceful-drain.sh gpu-node-128 --preserve-streams --grace=180` Starting.

marc.infra: Drain in progress. watch logs for aborted handshakes. If we see abort rate >2% we will pause and increase spill to 90%.

incident-bot: monitor-bot: scaling: us-east fallback scaled +8 pods to handle spill

marc.infra: Drain completed. Node evacuated. Tagging node: `kubectl label node gpu-node-128 incident.quarantine=true` and setting unschedulable.

oncall-sre: Post-evac metrics: global p99 1.4s, us-west p99 1.8s, p95 stable under 1.0s. Rolling back cross-region split to 85/15 in favor of west gradually over 20m.

kai.ops: Updating customer CT-9002 with resolution note and link to status page.

olivia.eng: Opening vendor support case with attached NVML traces and thermal graphs. Case VEND-445001. Requested expedited hardware swap. Also captured encrypted core dump per vendor suggests persistent memory errors on GPU memory channels.

rachel.pm: Assigning postmortem owners: olivia.eng + marc.infra. Deliverable: timeline, RCA (hardware root cause hypothesis), customer impact, gaps in streaming-drain runbook, and automation proposals. Due in 48h.

oncall-sre: Proposed automation items: (1) auto-divert rule when gpu.ecc.correctable_rate > 60 for 3m OR gpu.junction_temp > 90C for 2m, (2) automatic cross-region spill to configured fallback with throttled ramp and autoscale, (3) streaming-safe-drain script tested in staging to run non-disruptively.

olivia.eng: I'll draft the automation RFC and a quick PR for alert thresholds. Also adding an observability dashboard tile for NVML bus/error rates.

marc.infra: Created vendor ticket VEND-445001 and cloud case CLOUD-777888. Marked node for replacement and block scheduling until vendor confirms.

support-leo: Final customer update sent with CT-9002: "Service restored to normal; we've quarantined one GPU node and are replacing hardware. If you still see issues, please reply to this ticket."

oncall-sre: Handing off to marc.infra for overnight monitoring and vendor coordination. If p99 increases again, escalate to oncall immediately. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT ARCHIVE: Thread archived. Follow-ups: /incidents/6500000000/postmortem, automation ticket: infra/auto-divert-6500."
